instruction: Perform a rigorous GDPR Article 28 compliance review of this Data Processing Agreement. Verify: subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of processing, categories of data and data subjects, obligations and rights of the controller, and whether all mandatory Article 28(3) clauses are present and adequate.

elements.description: Processor provides sufficient guarantees of GDPR-compliant measures and rights protection.
Controller commits to use only processors meeting that guarantee threshold.
Prior specific or general written controller authorisation is required.
General authorisation includes advance notice of additions or replacements.
The controller has a meaningful opportunity to object.

selectionReasons: GDPR Article 28(3) chapeau mandates that processing by a processor shall be governed by a contract setting out the duration of the processing along with other mandatory particulars.

Article 28(3) chapeau mandates that every processing agreement set out the subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of processing, categories of personal data, categories of data subjects, and the controller's obligations and rights.

Covers mandatory processor agreement particulars under Article 28(3), including the subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of processing, type of personal data, categories of data subjects, and controller rights/obligations.

Covers the mandatory baseline requirements of GDPR Article 28(3) for processing agreements, including subject matter, duration, nature and purpose, types of personal data, categories of data subjects, and the obligations and rights of the controller.

Covers the general requirements for processing particulars (subject matter, duration, nature/purpose, categories of data/data subjects, and general rights/obligations) in DPA contracts under Article 28(3).

elements.description: The contract sets out the subject matter of the processing. Proven only by text stating what personal-data processing activity or service this agreement covers. A named cross-reference to another document counts only if that document itself is confirmed to state the subject matter.

The contract sets out the duration of the processing. Proven only by text stating how long the processing continues; termination rights or deletion timelines alone do not establish duration unless they also state or reference the processing term itself.
The contract sets out the nature AND purpose of the processing — both what activities are performed on the data and why. Either half alone is partial, not present.

The contract sets out the types of personal data processed. A general definition of what could qualify as personal or sensitive data does not prove which categories are actually processed under the services.
The contract sets out the categories of data subjects (who the data is about), distinct from what data is processed about them.
The contract sets out the controller's (not the processor's) obligations and rights — e.g. the duty to give lawful instructions or the right to audit the processor.

selectionReasons: Covers mandatory Article 28(3)(a) documented instructions requirement for processor agreements.

elements.description: The processor processes personal data only on documented instructions from the controller.
elements.proofGuidance: A clause using 'only on documented instructions' / 'in accordance with the Controller's written instructions'. May sit in an operational-obligations section, a jurisdiction addendum, or the international-transfers section.
nonProofTraps: 'As reasonably necessary to provide the Services' without an instruction-anchor.
A general confidentiality clause.
elements.remediationGuidance: Add the documented-instructions clause with the standard 28(3)(a) formulation.

elements.description: Instructions to make an international transfer are also processed only on documented instructions, unless required by law (with a notification obligation).
elements.applicabilityGuidance: Applies when the arrangement contemplates cross-border transfers of personal data. Absence of trigger words is not evidence of non-applicability.
elements.proofGuidance: The Article 28(3)(a) proviso: unless required by Union or Member State law, in which case the processor notifies the controller before processing (unless the law prohibits notification for important public-interest reasons).
nonProofTraps: A separate international-transfer clause that names the mechanism (SCCs) but not the instruction-based control.
elements.remediationGuidance: Add the proviso allowing law-mandated processing with a controller-notification obligation.

elements.description: Confidentiality of authorised persons (Art 28(3)(b))

selectionReasons: Covers mandatory Article 28(3)(c) security measures requirement for processor agreements.

elements.description: The processor is obligated to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data (a TOMs/security covenant, not a bare compliance aspiration).
elements.proofGuidance: An operative obligation on the processor to implement technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk — may reference Article 32 or 'appropriate security measures'.
nonProofTraps: A generic 'comply with Data Protection Laws' statement with no security-measures obligation.
A confidentiality clause with no technical/organisational security commitment.
elements.remediationGuidance: Add an Article 28(3)(c) / Article 32 security-measures obligation on the processor.

elements.description: The security commitment is substantiated — by named measures (encryption, access controls, resilience, testing) or by an incorporated security exhibit/schedule whose content is confirmed in the reviewed materials.
elements.proofGuidance: Substantive security content — enumerated controls, risk-appropriate measures, or a confirmed security exhibit/schedule. A bare pointer to 'the Information Security Exhibit' counts only if that exhibit is supplied and contains measures.
nonProofTraps: A bare cross-reference to an Information Security Exhibit or security schedule that is not supplied or confirmed to contain measures.
A one-line 'industry-standard security' promise with no measures, exhibit, or schedule.
elements.remediationGuidance: Substantiate the security obligation with named measures or attach/incorporate a security exhibit with actual controls.

selectionReasons: Covers mandatory Article 28(3)(d) subprocessor conditions and flow-down obligations.

elements.description: The processor must obtain the controller's prior general or specific written authorisation before engaging a subprocessor.
elements.proofGuidance: Prior written authorisation — specific (per subprocessor) or general (list + changes). 'May engage subprocessors' or notice-only language is not enough.
nonProofTraps: A clause that merely says the processor 'will notify' or 'may engage subprocessors' without prior authorisation.
A published subprocessor list with no authorisation mechanism.
elements.remediationGuidance: Require prior general or specific written authorisation before engaging any subprocessor.

elements.description: Where general authorisation applies, the controller receives advance notice of subprocessor changes and a meaningful opportunity to object.
elements.proofGuidance: Change-notice + objection window — typically 30 days' notice and a right to object before the new subprocessor processes data. Required when general (not specific-only) authorisation is used.
nonProofTraps: Notice of subprocessor changes with no objection right.
A post-hoc notification after the subprocessor is already engaged.
elements.remediationGuidance: Add advance notice and a meaningful objection opportunity for subprocessor changes under general authorisation.

elements.description: Each subprocessor is engaged under a written agreement imposing data-protection obligations on the subprocessor (equivalent engagement), not merely announced or listed.
elements.proofGuidance: Written subprocessor agreement / DPA requirement — the processor must impose contractual data-protection terms on subprocessors, not merely disclose their names.
nonProofTraps: A subprocessor list or registry with no written-agreement requirement.
Processor liability for subprocessor acts without a written engagement obligation.
elements.remediationGuidance: Require each subprocessor to be engaged under a written data-processing agreement.

elements.description: The processor provides substantive assistance to the controller, not only request forwarding
Assistance is delivered through appropriate technical or organisational measures where possible
Assistance covers the controller's response to data-subject rights requests

rule.title: Processor assistance with security, breach, DPIA, and consultation duties

elements.description: Assistance with controller security obligations under Article 32
Assistance with breach notification and communication under Articles 33-34
Assistance with DPIAs and prior consultation under Articles 35-36
The controller has a right to choose between deletion and return.
elements.proofGuidance: A clause explicitly giving the controller the choice (e.g. 'at the Controller's option, delete or return').
nonProofTraps: A deletion-only clause with no return branch.
A return-only clause with no deletion branch.
elements.remediationGuidance: Reword the post-termination clause to grant the controller a choice.

elements.description: The processor is obligated to delete on request.
elements.proofGuidance: A deletion obligation triggered at the end of services or on request.
nonProofTraps: A permission to delete rather than an obligation.
A discretion to retain 'for legitimate business purposes' with no boundary.
elements.remediationGuidance: Convert the retention discretion into a deletion obligation.

elements.description: The processor is obligated to return on request.
elements.proofGuidance: A return / export obligation triggered at the end of services or on request.
nonProofTraps: A migration-services offer priced separately, without an obligation.
elements.remediationGuidance: Add a return obligation (format specified where reasonable).

elements.description: The processor deletes existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage.
elements.proofGuidance: The 28(3)(g) closing proviso — retention only where required by law, with the residual data still subject to processor obligations.
nonProofTraps: Retention for 'business continuity' or 'audit' without a legal basis.
elements.remediationGuidance: Add the closing proviso limiting retention to legally required cases.

selectionReasons: Covers mandatory Article 28(3)(h) audit rights, compliance evidence, and unlawful instruction warnings.

rule.title: Compliance evidence, audits, and unlawful-instruction warning

elements.description: The processor must make available information necessary to demonstrate compliance AND allow for and contribute to audits and inspections by the controller or its mandated auditor.
elements.proofGuidance: Both limbs required — compliance information AND an actual audit/inspection right. Third-party certifications on request alone is partial.
nonProofTraps: Third-party certifications/reports (SOC2, ISO 27001) on request with no independent audit/inspection right.
An information-provision clause with no audit or inspection right.
An audit right limited to reviewing a summary report that cannot demonstrate compliance.
elements.remediationGuidance: Add both compliance-information access and a controller (or auditor) audit/inspection right with processor contribution.

elements.description: The processor must immediately inform the controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes GDPR or other data-protection provisions.
elements.proofGuidance: Article 28(3) closing sentence — immediate warning of unlawful instructions. Distinct from the documented-instructions clause in 28(3)(a).
nonProofTraps: A documented-instructions clause with no unlawful-instruction warning.
A general compliance cooperation clause with no immediate-inform duty.
elements.remediationGuidance: Add the immediate unlawful-instruction notification duty.

rule.title: Subprocessor equivalent obligations and processor liability

elements.description: The processor must impose on each subprocessor the same data-protection obligations imposed on the processor by the DPA — specifically by reference to the processor's Article 28(3) obligations.
elements.proofGuidance: Same-obligations covenant — 'impose the same data protection obligations', 'equivalent to those in this DPA', or reference to Article 28(3) obligations flowing down.
nonProofTraps: A general statement that subprocessors must comply with data protection law.
Processor liability for subprocessor acts without a same-obligations flow-down covenant.
elements.remediationGuidance: Require subprocessors to be bound by the same Article 28(3) obligations as the processor.

elements.description: Flow-down is evidenced as an actual contractual imposition on subprocessors (by contract, DPA, or equivalent written instrument), not merely asserted via processor liability.
elements.proofGuidance: Evidence that obligations are contractually imposed on subprocessors — written agreement, DPA, or explicit 'by contract' language. Liability alone does not prove flow-down.
nonProofTraps: Processor remains liable for subprocessor conduct with no contractual flow-down language.
A subprocessor list with no 'by written agreement' or 'by contract' imposition.
elements.remediationGuidance: Evidence contractual flow-down — require subprocessors to enter written agreements imposing the same obligations.

elements.description: The processor terms are contained or incorporated in a written or electronic instrument.
Processor status is limited to processing on the controller's behalf and instructions.
Determining purposes and means triggers controller responsibility for that processing.
